title.narrative: Kiwa Initiative – Nature Based Solutions for Climate Resilience

description.narrative: The Kiwa Initiative – Nature Based Solutions for Climate Resilience (formerly Pacific Initiative for Biodiversity and Climate Change) is a French-led initiative. The Initiative aims to strengthen resilience to climate change through biodiversity conservation for Pacific islands ecosystems, communities and economies. The French Development Agency (AFD) manage pooled donor funding, which will provide community, national and regional grants to PICTs and regional organisations (the Pacific Community SPC and Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP)), and International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). Over €79.5 million has been committed by five donors being France, European Union, New Zealand, Australia and Canada.

description.narrative: During 2023/2024 the Kiwa Initiative continued to fund seventeen local projects and five regional projects while also supporting regional capacity building through technical assistance provided by SPC and SPREP. Australia provided additional funding to support Kiwa activities. One of the regional projects, Pacific Organic Learning Farms Network, which commenced in May 2021, continued to deliver on the objectives of developing access to organic farming methods and technologies to address food security, climate change adaptation and biodiversity conservation. The project has facilitated the establishment of seven Organic Learning Farms based on the principles of nature-based solutions. 326 farmers successfully applied as First Circle farmers in November 2023, and are therefore eligible for training, peer to peer learning, business planning and certifications through the program.

description.narrative: INSPIRE (Invasive SpecIes Management for Resilient ecosystems and communities): Implemented by BirdLife International, INSPIRE has launched activities in Fiji (Gau Island), French Polynesia, Palau, and Samoa, focusing on biosecurity and invasive species management. Key achievements include conserving/protecting 640 hectares of land and restoring 213.5 hectares of habitat. Significant progress was made in controlling invasive species, with 390 African Tulip trees treated in Fiji and 37,821 invasive plants treated/removed in French Polynesia. Over 160 individuals were trained in invasive species management.

description.narrative: In 2023/2024 Australia made an additional contribution of $5,000,000.00 to the multi-donor funded Kiwa Initiative. During the reporting period, Kiwa launched the MiCOAST program, which will contribute to the implementation of the Pacific Framework for Action for Scaling up Community-based Fisheries Management at twelves sites in six Micronesian jurisdictions by enhancing the sustainability and resiliency of coastal fisheries, thereby safeguarding the well-being of local communities and their reliance on valuable marine resources.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: MiCOAST (Micronesia Community-based Fisheries Management as a Nature-based Solution for Coastal Resilience): Led by OneReef, MiCOAST is focused on scaling up community-based fisheries management (CBFM) and nature-based solutions (NbS) in Micronesia. The project has steadily increased momentum, initiating groundwork, engaging communities, and implementing climate-adaptive interventions. At least 1,023 individuals have directly benefited from project activities, with a near-equal distribution of male and female participants. Progress was made in revising fisheries and natural resource management plans and activating community outreach campaigns.

description.narrative: PEBACC+ (Pacific Ecosystem-based Adaptation to Climate Change – Plus ): Implemented by SPREP, PEBACC+ has made strides in ecosystem-based adaptation across Vanuatu, Fiji, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Wallis-et-Futuna. Activities include the restoration of 206 hectares of forests, mangroves, coastline and riverbanks. The project has conducted 6 targeted training sessions to enhance community capacity in Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and sustainable resource management. Progress was made in mainstreaming EbA and NbS into national and sub-national development policies.

The RESTORE Project (Restoring Ecosystems for Sustainable, Transformative and Resilient Communities.): RESTORE was launched in July 2024 and is rapidly establishing foundations for ecosystem restoration and community resilience across Fiji, Samoa, and Timor-Leste. The project conducted inception meetings in each country. Fiji, key activities included workshops, dialogues with 180 community members (50% women), and restoring 9 hectares of mangroves. Samoa initiated stakeholder engagement through district-level workshops (February 2025) engaging over 100 individuals (60% women and youth). Timor-Leste saw rapid start-up with national policy alignment and baseline data collection in 4 villages. A Pacific Accountability and Grievance Mechanism was launched, and a regional knowledge exchange was hosted in Fiji in partnership with SPREP. ‍ The project has exceeded gender inclusion targets as part of consultation processes across all implementation countries: ‍ • Fiji achieved greater than 50% female participation in consultations with three women's groups engaged in livelihoods activities, with cofinancing from the Fiji Blue Carbon Project ‍ • Samoa maintained 60% women and youth participation in all engagements ‍ • Timor-Leste reached 65% female engagement in consultations while establishing four women-led village committees. ‍ Timor-Leste's achievement of integrating gender into community by-laws in three villages demonstrates the project's transformative potential for inclusive governance.
